problems.title: Trace two-sum
problems.statement: nums = [4, 1, 5, 3], target = 8, one pass with a map value → index, query before insert.

parts.prompt: At which index i is the pair found?
Size of the map when it's found?

problems.solution: i = 0 (4: need 4, absent; insert), i = 1 (1: need 7), i = 2 (5: need 3), i = 3 (3: need 5, found at index 2). The map has 3 entries.

problems.title: Choosing a key
problems.statement: Group strings that are rotations of each other ("abc", "bca", "cab").
hints: Sorted letters also group anagrams that aren't rotations ("acb").
problems.solution: Sorted letters over-group; the smallest rotation is equal exactly for rotations.

problems.title: Space for time

parts.prompt: A Python set of them uses roughly…
options: tens of MB (object overhead per entry)

hints: Python ints and hash slots carry overhead.
problems.solution: 4 MB raw; a Python set uses roughly 30–60 MB. In C++ an unordered_set is also several times the raw size. Mention memory when it's large.

problems.title: Counts not maps
problems.statement: Check whether two lowercase strings are anagrams.
problems.solution: An int[26]: one increment per character of one string, one decrement per character of the other, then check all zero. O(n), tiny constant.

problems.title: Longest consecutive: amortised

parts.prompt: How many elements start a walk?
Total successor checks (y + 1 in set) including the failing one?

problems.solution: Only 1 starts: it checks 2, 3, 4, 5 (found) and 6 (absent): 5 checks. Without the rule, each element would walk its own suffix: 15 checks.

problems.title: Top-k approaches
problems.statement: Top 10 most frequent among n = 10⁷ items with 10⁶ distinct values.

options: A size-10 min-heap over the counts

hints: k is tiny; buckets would be 10⁷ long.
problems.solution: A heap of size 10 costs O(d log 10) over d distinct values; buckets need an array as long as n. Choose by k and n.

problems.title: Design under memory limits
problems.statement: Detect duplicates among 10⁹ 64-bit IDs streaming past, with 1 GB of RAM.

options: A hash set of all IDs (8 GB+)

parts.prompt: If a small false-positive rate is acceptable?

problems.solution: Exact: sort externally (or hash-partition to disk, then dedupe each partition in memory). Approximate: a Bloom filter at ~10 bits per item ≈ 1.25 GB for ~1% false positives.

problems.title: Query before insert
problems.statement: Two-sum with nums = [3, 3], target = 6, but the code inserts before querying and checks only membership.

parts.prompt: What does it return for nums = [3], target = 6?

problems.solution: Inserting first lets an element match itself. Query first, then insert.
